Bounded ownership and fit-cache benchmark

Source: vignettes/articles/contributor-tools-hardening-benchmark-readme.Rmd
contributor-tools-hardening-benchmark-readme.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

Run from the repository root with:

Rscript tools/hardening/benchmark/benchmark-boundaries.R

The committed results/ snapshot measures the current source loaded by pkgload at frozen candidate 169c16e4ba00c687c1f03fe37e9d79a11d01cd8f, on local Apple arm64, R 4.6.0 and data.table 1.18.4. metadata.R records the UTC run time and environment. source-hashes.csv and the RDS metadata identify every R source file and this benchmark script by MD5; source stability is checked between load and completed measurements; the recorded Git HEAD is context, not the identity of the uncommitted implementation. An optional SCEPTRE_BENCH_LIBRARY selects an installed package instead.

Ownership boundaries

Each latency uses 20 batches of 10 serialize/unserialize ownership copies. The allocation profile measures one additional copy, with no baseline subtraction. Values below are the final run; CSVs retain the unrounded measurements.

Workload Input object.size bytes Median copy, ms Observed batch-average range, ms Profiled allocation bytes
Actual five-row result table 4,880 <0.1 0–0.1 11,328
Actual saved record including history 48,464 0.10 0–0.10 25,880
Actual CRT output_amount=3 record 1,264,216 1.50 1.40–2.00 566,288
Synthetic nested draw graph 591,264 0.75 0.70–2.60 1,091,048

The synthetic graph is not scientific output level 3: it contains 500 rows of 128 arbitrary normal draws (64,000 numeric values), a nested data.table attribute, and a genuine frozen RunPlan. The actual CRT record is measured separately. The tiny table’s zero batch averages reflect clock resolution, not a zero-cost copy.

Rprofmem() reports recorded R allocations, not peak resident memory, retained memory, native allocations or whole-workflow memory. object.size() is an R estimate that can count shared content repeatedly; allocation totals and object sizes need not agree. One profile does not establish a general memory bound. Serialization temporarily materializes a serialized buffer and an owned graph; these measurements do not qualify arbitrarily large nested result histories. Cleanup disables profiling/removes temporary profiles and removes fit traces on both success and error.

Cold and warm CRT

The real high-MOI complement-control CRT fixture has 160 source cells, 155 retained cells and five requested pairs; its plan uses B1=499, B2=4999 and B3=0 with output level 3. Both runs use seed 172839. Exact result values, saved fit values and warnings agree between cold and warm runs.

Path Actual response-fit calls Actual perturbation-fit calls Three elapsed times, seconds
Cold, prepared screen 4 2 0.146, 0.144, 0.154
Warm, completed cached screen 0 0 0.146, 0.154, 0.156

Fit-call counts are measured separately with tracing; the timings are uninstrumented. They establish that compatible warm fits are reused. The tiny fixture’s elapsed times are noisy and effectively comparable; this is not a speedup claim. The process/filesystem are already warm, there are only three repetitions, and all public validation, draw generation, inference and ownership work remains included. No large-screen, cross-platform, distributed-process or peak-memory conclusion follows from this local benchmark.

Raw artifacts are copy-boundaries.csv, crt-cache-times.csv, crt-fit-counts.csv, source-hashes.csv, metadata.R and benchmark-results.rds under results/.
